newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Lenco says in talks, no comment on Malbak.
newsitem.headline: Lenco says in talks, no comment on Malbak.

text.p: Lenco Holdings, the packaging firm in the Rembrandt Group Ltd (Remgro) stable which has been linked with a possible takeover of Malbak Ltd, said it could not comment on the rumoured deal.

"People have speculated very widely and in truth some of them are quite close, while others are far off...But other than that I can say nothing," Douglas de Jager, Lenco's executive chairman told Reuters.
He said Lenco was involved in some talks, leading to a cautionary notice to shareholders on May 20. That brief announcement said Lenco was in unspecified discussions.
"I would not have put out a cautionary if nothing was going on..(But) the talks are at a very sensitive stage, there are lots of human beings involved," de Jager said.
He declined to comment whether the talks were linked with fellow packaging group Malbak, which on Thursday issued a cautionary saying it was in unspecified talks.
Following a report in a Sunday newspaper, the Johannesburg bourse has been awash with speculation that Remgro is set to buy Malbak, in which it already holds an 18 percent stake.
The Business Times newspaper said Remgro may merge Malbak with its packaging operations held through a 30 percent stake in Printpak and a 17 percent stake in Lenco.
Remgro managing director Thys Visser earlier also declined to comment on the talk.
The paper said that it was "common knowledge in the market" that Remgro was eyeing Malbak, which recently underwent a rigorous unbundling exercise which has left it as a focused packaging company.
Malbak's primary assets since its unbundling are a 68 percent stake in Kohler Ltd and a 64 percent interest in UK-listed MY Holdings Plc.

Malbak shares jumped almost seven percent or 46 cents on Thursday to 724 cents in busy trade of 754,200 shares on the rumours. Lenco was 85 cents better at 700 cents but Remgro finished the day unchanged at 46.00 rand.
